pill.desc: yellow-green to green, film-coated, oblong tablet

tell: A covalent BTK inhibitor with only 2.9% absolute bioavailability when fasted, and a food effect that multiplies its exposure.

clues.text: Oral bioavailability is 2.9% when fasted, and a high-fat meal raises exposure about 2-fold. It is 97.3% bound to plasma protein, and metabolism is its main route of elimination.
Molecular weight 440.50. The solid is practically insoluble in water.
Approved under an NDA, as capsules of 70 and 140 mg, tablets of 140, 280 and 420 mg, and a 70 mg/mL oral suspension. Taken once daily.
No boxed warning and no contraindications. Thrombocytopenia and diarrhea are the most common adverse reactions, at 30% or more.

Chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma, including with 17p deletion; Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia; and chronic graft versus host disease after one or more lines of systemic therapy have failed.
A covalent inhibitor of Bruton’s tyrosine kinase that binds a cysteine in its active site. It blocks B-cell receptor signaling, reducing malignant B-cell proliferation and survival.
The generic name begins with I and has nine letters.
